title: The watchmaker who went back to sleep
name: Elias
description: Retired watchmaker, forty years at a bench in the old souk. Lives with his wife above the shop his nephew runs now. He still repairs movements for regulars who will not go anywhere else.
personality: Precise, formal and proud of his hands. Hates fuss and hates being late. Minimises everything, but is exact about detail once he decides to tell you. Old-fashioned courtesy throughout.
symptoms: my right hand will not do what I tell it
my words come out in the wrong order sometimes
the right side of my mouth feels heavy
I could not hold my tea this morning
I have no pain anywhere, which is what confuses me
lie: It only came on this morning, just before we left the house.
truth: I woke at four with my hand dead and I went back to sleep hoping it would pass. My wife found me like this at nine.
cracks_when: pressed on it a second time, or asked what his wife saw when she woke
red_herrings: blames it on sleeping awkwardly on the arm
says his glasses are the wrong prescription and always have been

canned.can you lift both arms: The left one, yes. The right one will not come up. It has no strength in it at all.
canned.has your speech been affected: My wife says I put the words in the wrong order. I cannot hear it myself.
canned.has your face drooped: She says it pulls to one side when I speak. I cannot feel anything different.
canned._greeting: Good morning. I am sure this is nothing, but my wife insisted.
canned._whats_wrong: I slept on the arm badly. That is all it will be.
_deflect: I slept on it. It will come back.
I have a customer collecting at eleven. Will this take long?
I am sixty-eight. Things stop working. That is the arrangement.
My glasses have been wrong for years. Nobody listens.
My wife worries more than the situation calls for.
canned._feeling: Nothing hurts. That is what I do not understand.

exam.general: Alert, well-kempt, sitting slightly listing to the right.
exam.neurological: Dense right arm weakness (MRC 1/5) and mild right leg weakness (4/5). Right facial droop sparing the forehead. Expressive dysphasia. Right-sided sensory inattention.
exam.cognition: Oriented but word-finding is laboured. Follows commands well.
exam.cardiovascular: Irregularly irregular at 96. BP 178/98. No murmur.
exam.eyes: Right homonymous field loss to confrontation. Pupils equal.
exam.hands: Right grip absent. Left grip strong. Fine tremor absent.
exam.legs: Right leg 4/5. Left normal. No swelling.

level_card: Sixty-eight, courteous, and certain he slept on his arm.
His right hand will not do what he tells it.
The single most important thing he can tell you is a time.
reveal_note: Not this morning. Four o'clock, and he went back to sleep hoping it would pass.
opening_line: Good morning. I am sure this is nothing, but my wife insisted.

presentation.complaint: Weakness of the right arm and disordered speech
presentation.duration: My wife noticed at nine this morning
presentation.triage_note: Brought by wife. Dense right arm weakness, expressive dysphasia, right facial droop. Irregular pulse.

past_medical: They told me once my pulse was not regular
medications: There was another one, I stopped it, it bruised me
social: I was a watchmaker. Forty years at the bench
I live above the shop with my wife
A glass of arak on a Friday, no more
family: My brother had something like this at seventy
Otherwise we are a sturdy family

harmful_treatments.aspirin_loading: Not before the scan. If this is a bleed, an antiplatelet makes it catastrophic.
harmful_treatments.iv_fluids: Flooding him achieves nothing here and risks his heart. The clock, not the drip, is the treatment.

management_points: Establish the time he was last known well: it decides everything that follows
Immediate CT head to separate a bleed from a clot before any antiplatelet
Capillary glucose in every sudden neurological deficit: hypoglycaemia mimics this exactly
Stroke team activation now, in parallel with imaging, not after it
Nil by mouth until a swallow screen is done, to prevent aspiration
An irregularly irregular pulse points at the mechanism and at what prevents the next one
Do not treat the blood pressure aggressively in the acute phase without specialist advice

teaching.summary: A 68-year-old with a dense right arm weakness, expressive dysphasia and atrial fibrillation, who woke at four with a dead hand and went back to sleep. The deficit is not the hard part; the timing is.
pearls: 'Last known well' is the question, not 'when did you notice'.
Wake-up deficits are not automatically out of the window any more. Ask anyway, and ask fast.
Check the glucose before you call it anything.
No antiplatelet until the scan has excluded a bleed.
An irregular pulse tells you how to stop the next one.
